newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty safe below c.bank territory, but may rise.
newsitem.headline: Zloty safe below c.bank territory, but may rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty hovered safely below central bank intervention levels in quiet early trade as foreign investors searched in vain to buy T-bills with zlotys obtained from deals from the last three days, dealers said.

On Thursday, Friday and Monday the central bank bought an estimated $340 million to stop the zloty's rise which was fuelled by foreign entry into Polish T-bills as yields began topping out after weeks of rises.
"Some foreign investors may have exchanged more currencies into zlotys then they managed to spend at the Monday T-bill primary tender," said Bartlomiej Kumela of Societe Generale.
"They are now trying to find paper on the secondary market, but there are very few offers, and yields fell dramatically."
Dealers said offers of the 52-week paper dropped to 21.15 percent from the average yield of 21.68 percent at the primary tender and even offers of 21.00 percent were taken up.
"Many banks may have failed to get the longer-term paper at yesterday's tender and are now desperate to buy it, but there is none," said Rafal Chodzidlo of Bank Slaski SA.
Delears also said some banks might have short currency positions after three days of central bank currency buying and might try to rebuild them today, pushing the zloty lower.
"Many banks may be short in currencies now and may be trying to rebuild positions which would keep the zloty down," said Leszek Szafranek of Bank Slaski SA.
But others said the zloty's weak start could be deceptive.
"The low opening and quiet market deos not have to mean it will stay that way. We may still see some action later today," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.

On the money market bids for overnight cash plunged more than eight points to 12.00/20.00 while tomorrow/next rates fell four points to 17.00/22.00 percent as the market was swamped with zlotys created by central bank currency purchases.

The NBP offered a massive 2.2 billion zloty 14-day reverse repo with T/N value date and a 800 million zloty sale of its 91-day bills with O/N value date to drain the excess liquidity, but call money rtaes refused to budge.
"T/N rates may inch slightly higher, but O/N cash is likely to stay low for the rest of the day," one dealer said.
